name: xn_anim_rand_seed
evidence: Copies the BIOS tick count (word at 46Ch) into D_000C0030, the LCG state only C0307 uses (through C02E9, from ASCR opcodes 0 and 7). init_video calls it once.

name: xn_anim_reset
evidence: Resets an ASCR animation struct (monster+0x2C1): frame +0/+2, events/flags word +10h, wait +12h, facing +15h, record +16h, script pos +8 to 0, byte +13h to FFh; keeps script +4, step divisor +0Ch, request +14h. monster_init and load_relink_character call it.

name: xn_anim_reset_with_rate
evidence: xn_anim_reset (C010F) then word [eax+0Ch] = dx, the tick divisor C019C uses. Nothing references it (found_by unreferenced).

name: xn_anim_update
evidence: object_draw_cb calls it for each type-18 creature per frame: a pending anim_request (+14h != FFh) starts when the script is idle, waiting or at opcode 3/4 (entry word script+6+2*req, 8000h = state 0; anim_current = req, request = FFh); then steps C019C.

name: xn_anim_tick
evidence: step = D_001343C0 / word +0Ch; returns CF when it equals the last step (+0Eh). Otherwise counts the wait byte +12h down (FFh holds) or, at 0, runs the opcodes (C01EB) from the script pointer +8 and stores the new pointer. Only caller C013B.

name: xn_anim_run_opcodes
evidence: The ASCR interpreter loop (esi = struct, edi = script pos): a byte >= 0 calls handler D_000C0000[op] until one returns CF; a negative byte b is a frame (frame = -b-1 into +0 and +2) and ends the step. Only caller C019C.

name: xn_anim_op_loop_start
evidence: ASCR opcode 0 (D_000C0000[0]), 4 bytes op,min,max,counter: stores a random count in [min,max] (C02E9) into the script's own byte +3, which opcode 1 counts down. No MONSTER.BSA script uses it (static walk of the 60 ASCR records).

name: xn_anim_op_loop_end
evidence: ASCR opcode 1, 3 bytes op + word offset of an opcode 0: decrements that opcode's counter byte +3 and jumps to just after it while non-zero, else falls through. No MONSTER.BSA script uses it (static walk of the 60 ASCR records).

name: xn_anim_op_set_events
evidence: ASCR opcode 2, 3 bytes: ORs its word into +10h (anim_events: bit 0 strike, bit 1 missile release; exp_c1: ai_update_creatures clears bit 0 and calls weapon_melee_strike). 7 play episodes.

name: xn_anim_op_set_byte13
evidence: ASCR opcode 10, 2 bytes: stores its operand in byte +13h of the anim struct (C010F sets it to FFh). No reader of +13h in XnGine or the game C. No MONSTER.BSA script uses it (static walk of the 60 ASCR records).

name: xn_anim_op_set_mirror
evidence: ASCR opcode 9, 2 bytes: clears bit 15 of word +10h and sets it when the operand is non-zero (anim_flags bit 7, the mirrored view monster_set_action also writes). No MONSTER.BSA script uses it (static walk of the 60 ASCR records).

name: xn_anim_op_restart
evidence: ASCR opcode 5: computes script + word[script+2] but stores the bare offset into +8 and continues from it as a pointer (a bug). No MONSTER.BSA script uses it (static walk of the 60 ASCR records).

name: xn_anim_op_stop
evidence: ASCR opcode 6, 1 byte: edi = 0 and CF; C019C stores 0 as the script pointer, so the script ends and the creature holds its frame. No MONSTER.BSA script uses it (static walk of the 60 ASCR records).

name: xn_anim_op_frame_wait
evidence: ASCR opcode 3, 3 bytes: frame into +0 and +2, wait count into +12h (0 becomes FFh = hold), returns CF so the step ends; C013B lets a new request interrupt here. 21 play episodes.

name: xn_anim_op_goto
evidence: ASCR opcode 4, 3 bytes: continues at script + word operand (C013B also lets a new request interrupt at this opcode); 377 uses in MONSTER.BSA, ending every state's loop.

name: xn_anim_op_goto_random
evidence: ASCR opcode 7, 4 bytes op,percent,word offset: jumps to script+offset when a random 0..100 (C02E9 with ax=6400h) is <= percent, else skips. 54 uses in MONSTER.BSA (static walk).

name: xn_anim_op_goto_if_events
evidence: ASCR opcode 8, 5 bytes op, word mask, word offset: jumps to script+offset when word +10h & mask is non-zero, else skips. No MONSTER.BSA script uses it (static walk of the 60 ASCR records).

name: xn_anim_op_set_record
evidence: ASCR opcode 11, 2 bytes: operand into +16h (anim_record, the texture record group: 0 move, 5 attack, 15 idle, 20 spell per exp_c1); object_draw_cb adds anim_facing to pick the image. 37 play episodes.

name: xn_anim_rand_range
evidence: al = lo, ah = hi: returns lo + (C0307 & 7Fh) mod (hi-lo+1) in ax. Callers: ASCR opcodes 0 (loop count) and 7 (0..100).

name: xn_anim_rand_next
evidence: 16-bit LCG: D_000C0030 = D_000C0030*05E5h + 29h, returned in ax. Only caller C02E9.

name: xn_sys_crit_error_handler
evidence: Protected-mode int 24h (DOS critical error) handler: mov eax,1 (AL = 1, retry) and iretd. C0520 installs it, C0580 puts the old vector back; the tracer saw it run (found by run time).

name: xn_sys_install_crit_error_handler

name: xn_sys_restore_crit_error_handler

name: xn_draw_image_scaled

name: xn_draw_image_scaled_clip

name: xn_draw_image_scaled_row

name: xn_img_unpack_rows

name: xn_dos_make_path

name: xn_vid_play
evidence: (path, x, y, skippable): plays a VID movie at x,y with the clip rect set to it; 0 and CF if the file is missing, else 1; skippable stops on a mouse button or key. intro_play_logo, intro_play_movie, play_death_video, rest_close, quest_run_opcodes (ANIM*.VID).

name: xn_vid_open
evidence: Sets up a movie: read buffer big_buffer (FA00h), two locked 4000h audio buffers, the 60 Hz callback C1CDC (sound_timer_add), opens the file, reads the 15-byte header into D_000C1000 (frames +5, width +7, height +9, delay +0Bh, flags +0Dh), fills the buffer, decodes frame 1.

name: xn_vid_update
evidence: One pass of xn_vid_play's loop: while audio streams (state 3) waits for the sample-done flag D_000C1123 (restarting the sample if asked), otherwise for the 60 Hz countdown D_000C1466; stops the sound when the stream ran out of audio (D_000C1122), then decodes the next chunk (C18A3).

name: xn_vid_finish
evidence: End of a movie: stops the audio (C1D4D), unlocks and frees both audio buffers, closes the file unless header flag bit 0 (C1B1A), sets the done flag D_000C1453 and removes the timer (sound_timer_remove).

name: xn_vid_decode_chunk
evidence: Decodes the next VID chunk to the screen: 0 raw frame, 1 skip/copy delta, 4 delta from a start row, 3 RLE fill/copy, 2 palette (768 bytes to ports 3C8h/3C9h and D_000C1125), 7Ch audio header, 7Dh audio data, anything else ends (C1844).

name: xn_vid_close_file
evidence: Sets the audio state D_000C10FF to 0 and closes the movie file D_000C142B (int 21h 3Eh) if it is open. Only caller C1844.

name: xn_vid_refill
evidence: Moves the unread bytes (esi up to the buffer end) to the start of the read buffer D_000C1431 and reads the file into the rest (int 21h 3Fh); returns esi = buffer start. The decoder calls it near D_000C143D.

name: xn_vid_fill
evidence: First read of FA00h bytes of the movie into the read buffer D_000C1431; the read pointer D_000C1435 = buffer start. Only caller C1654.

name: xn_vid_schedule_frame
evidence: Adds the chunk's delay plus the header delay to the 60 Hz countdown D_000C1466; on the first frame after an audio header starts the sound (C1D6E) or arms its delay. Holds the 7Ch audio-header handler L_0C1BFD (rate = 1000000/(256-byte)).

name: xn_vid_read_audio
evidence: Copies an audio chunk (word length) out of the read buffer, refilling it as needed, into the next of the two 4000h audio buffers (D_000C1112/D_000C111A, lengths D_000C1116/D_000C111E) and toggles D_000C1100.

name: xn_vid_timer_cb
evidence: The 60 Hz timer callback xn_vid_open registers with sound_timer_add: decrements the frame countdown D_000C1466 and, when armed (D_000C146A), the audio delay D_000C1468.

name: xn_vid_audio_done_cb
evidence: SOS sample callback (stored at D_000C106B in the sample struct): points the struct (stack argument) at the other audio buffer and length and sets D_000C1123; if the last swap was not yet taken sets D_000C1124 so C17D6 restarts the sample.

name: xn_vid_audio_stop
evidence: When audio is active (D_000C10FF != 0): state 0 and stops sample D_000C1101 on the SOS digital driver D_0018DD60 (0xA2687).

name: xn_vid_audio_start
evidence: Fills the SOS start-sample struct D_000C100F (last buffer read and its length, rate D_000C1105, 8 bits, mono, volume 7F00h, callback C1D00) and starts it on driver D_0018DD60 (0xA2504); the handle goes to D_000C1101.

name: xn_vec_unit_direction
evidence: (from, to, out): unit vector from 'from' to 'to' (normalised by 14BDF7, 1.0 = 4000h) into out; returns out, or 0 when the points coincide. cast_fire_missile, cast_creature_missile, weapon_fire_arrow, weapon_monster_arrow set missile directions with it.

name: xn_vec_advance
